title: Investigatio motuum, quibus laminae et virgae elasticae contremiscunt

deep.reconstruction:
Context (§43–44 of E526): Euler is treating the transverse vibrations of a uniform elastic rod clamped (fixed in position and direction) at both ends. He writes the spatial factor as y = α e^{s/f} + β e^{-s/f} + γ sin(s/f) + δ cos(s/f), with ω = a/f and u = s/a.

The conditions at s = 0 are y(0) = y'(0) = 0, giving δ = −α−β and γ = −α+β. The conditions at s = a are y(a) = y'(a) = 0, giving the exact frequency equation cos ω = 2/(e^ω+e^{-ω}), i.e. cos ω cosh ω = 1. This is the same equation as in his 'first case', so the clamped–clamped rod has the same spectrum as that case. Euler takes the roots as ω = 3π/2, 5π/2, 7π/2, …

With α = 1 and β = ∓e^ω, the mode is X(u) = e^{uω} ∓ e^{ω(1−u)} − (1±e^ω) sin uω − (1∓e^ω) cos uω. The upper or lower sign is chosen by the sign of sin ω.

On this page he writes the general motion as a modal superposition: y = Σ C_k sin(ζ_k + t ω_k² c√(2gb)/a²) X_k(u). The angular frequency is proportional to ω² c/a², where c is the thickness parameter.

Corollary 1 (§44): the frequencies agree with case 1, but the shape is 'toto coelo diversa'. For the fundamental he takes ω = 3π/2 (sin ω < 0, lower signs) and e^ω ≈ 111, so X = e^{uω} + e^{ω(1−u)} − (1−e^ω) sin uω − (1+e^ω) cos uω. He evaluates at u = 1/3 and u = 2/3:
- u = 1/3, uω = π/2: X ≈ 4.8104 + 23.077 + 110 ≈ 138.
- u = 2/3, uω = π: X ≈ 23.140 + 4.810 + 112 = 140.

He asserts that a more accurate calculation would make the two values equal. That is what symmetry of the fundamental clamped–clamped mode requires. The curve is the nodeless arch ErsF of Tab. III Fig. 4. The next page adds that higher tones bring in 1, 2, 3 interior nodes successively.
errors: The roots of cos ω cosh ω = 1 are 4.7300, 7.8532, 10.9956, …, not exactly (2n+1)π/2. Euler presents 3π/2, 5π/2, … as 'the' values; they are only asymptotic approximations, poor for the fundamental (about 0.4% in ω, about 0.8% in frequency).

The discrepancy 138 vs 140 is not mainly an arithmetic-rounding issue. With ω = 3π/2 exactly, the mode is genuinely asymmetric: the values are about 138.27 vs 140.27 even with e^ω = 111.32. With the exact root ω = 4.73004, both evaluations give about 141.22. So Euler's claim of equality is correct, but only because the true root differs from 3π/2, not because of more decimal places.
He uses e^{ω(1−u)} = 111 × 0.2079 ≈ 23.077 at u = 1/3, instead of e^π = 23.1407; this is a minor rounding inconsistency (he uses 23.140 in case II).
Slip in the original text: 'ipsi ω tribuamus duos valores 1/3 et 2/3' should read 'ipsi u'.

ideas.what: Frequency equation cos ω cosh ω = 1 for a clamped–clamped beam, and the observation that it coincides with that of another boundary case, while the mode shapes differ
ideas.modern_name: Euler–Bernoulli beam eigenproblem; isospectrality of clamped–clamped and free–free beams (nonzero spectrum)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler and Daniel Bernoulli (1730s–1740s); Euler's systematic six-case treatment in E526
ideas.where_published: E526 itself; related earlier treatment in the Additamentum I to the Methodus inveniendi (E65, 1744)

ideas.what: General motion written as a superposition of simple harmonic modes with arbitrary amplitudes and phases
ideas.where_published: E526; Euler's string and rod papers

ideas.what: Remark that the clamped–clamped mode differs from the case-1 mode only by flipping the signs of the trigonometric coefficients γ, δ, i.e. replacing y by y''/k²
ideas.modern_name: Duality: second derivative of a free–free mode is a clamped–clamped mode
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard modern beam theory, e.g. Gladwell's inverse problems in vibration (attribution uncertain)
ideas.where_published: Implicit in E526 §43 (previous page); not stated as a derivative relation

ideas.what: Numerical evaluation of the fundamental mode shape at u = 1/3, 2/3 and the symmetry check

missed.claim: Euler notes that the clamped–clamped mode differs from the case-1 mode only by reversed signs of the sin/cos coefficients. This is exactly the statement y_cc ∝ y_ff'', which explains why the two cases are isospectral. He records the coincidence of frequencies and the sign flip, but does not state the derivative relation that explains it. The duality is well known today, so this is at most an early implicit appearance, not a missed result.
missed.quote: Quanquam autem omnes motus cum casu primo perfecte conueniunt: tamen figura, quam virga inter vibrandum recipit, toto coelo est diuersa.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority note only; possibly the earliest explicit observation of clamped/free isospectrality with distinct modes.

deep.surprise_reason: This is standard Euler–Bernoulli beam material that Euler systematised in E526 and that is well documented. The only subtlety is that his symmetry claim holds for the exact root but not for his approximation 3π/2, which is a minor historical-numerical footnote.
transcription_corrections: 'y = - - - - e^{uω}' — the dashes are typographic spacing (filler), not minus signs; read y = e^{uω} + e^{ω(1−u)} − (1−e^ω) sin uω − (1+e^ω) cos uω.
'ipsi ω tribuamus' is as printed; it is Euler's slip for u.
fin./cof. are the long-s renderings of sin./cos.
